Build parameter-estimation and cross-validation data for five GBLUP scenarios

Source: R/cv_scenarios.R
cv_scenarios.Rd

One call builds, from a single phenotype table, the data for the usual comparison of genomic prediction models across traits and groups (herds, lines, ...), all validated on the same individuals via one fold table:

scenariomodelparameter datatraining set
st_spsingle-trait, single grouptrait x grouptarget group
st_mpsingle-trait, groups combinedtraittarget group + all other groups
mt_sptwo-trait, single grouptrait pair x grouptarget group
mt_mptwo-trait, groups combinedtrait pairtarget group + all other groups
mt_btone trait treated as a different trait in each grouptraittarget group + all other groups

Every data file keeps all non-trait columns (including group) in their original order, and rows with missing phenotypes are kept, so the file layout is identical across scenarios.

cv_scenarios(
  data,
  cols,
  id,
  group,
  folds = NULL,
  v = 5L,
  repeats = 1L,
  strata = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  scenarios = c("st_sp", "st_mp", "mt_sp", "mt_mp", "mt_bt"),
  out_type = "dt"
)

Arguments

data

Phenotype table, one row per individual (or per record).

cols

Trait columns (names or indices).

id

Individual ID column.

group

A single grouping column (e.g. "test_herd").

folds

Optional fold table from cv_folds(); created from v, repeats, strata and seed when NULL.

v

Number of folds (>= 2).

repeats

Number of repeats (>= 1).

strata

Optional column to stratify on (must be constant within an individual). Numeric columns are binned into breaks quantile bins and strata smaller than pool are merged, as in split_cv().

seed

Optional seed; the global random number stream is left untouched.

scenarios

Scenarios to build (default: all five).

out_type

"dt" or "df" for the nested subsets.

Value

A list of class mintyr_scenarios: folds, and for each scenario a list with param (nested data for parameter estimation) and cv (output of apply_folds()). Write it out with export_scenarios().

See also

cv_folds(), apply_folds(), export_scenarios()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dat <- data.frame(id = paste0("i", 1:60), herd = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 30),
                  sex = sample(c("M", "F"), 60, TRUE),
                  adg = rnorm(60), bf = rnorm(60), fcr = rnorm(60))
sc <- cv_scenarios(dat, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), id = "id",
                   group = "herd", v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 123)
sc
#> <mintyr_scenarios> 60 individuals, 2 x 5
#>   st_sp  param:   6 data sets | cv:   60 train/validate pairs
#>   st_mp  param:   3 data sets | cv:   60 train/validate pairs
#>   mt_sp  param:   6 data sets | cv:   60 train/validate pairs
#>   mt_mp  param:   3 data sets | cv:   60 train/validate pairs
#>   mt_bt  param:   3 data sets | cv:   60 train/validate pairs
sc$mt_bt$cv$train[[1]]
